findings.title: SQL injection in migration via string interpolation of host values
findings.body: The migration interpolates the value of `h` (from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting) directly into a raw SQL INSERT statement without any escaping or parameterization. If the stored setting value contains single quotes or other SQL metacharacters, this allows SQL injection. Use `execute sanitize_sql_array(...)` or a parameterized query instead.

findings.title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil on failure paths
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns the boolean `false` (lines 12 and 15) when the URI is invalid or the host is blank, rather than `nil`. While current callers use `.present?` or `.try(:category_id)` which happen to work with `false`, this is semantically wrong for a finder method. Any future caller that does `record_for_host(url).category_id` without `.try` will get a `NoMethodError` on `false`. Return `nil` instead.

findings.title: destroy action does not handle missing record, causing NoMethodError
findings.body: In the `destroy` action, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` if no record matches. Calling `host.destroy` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 error. The same issue exists in `update` (line 10) where `save_host(host)` will fail on a nil host. Add a nil check or use `find` with a rescue to return a 404.

findings.title: before_validation callback crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` without checking if `self.host` is nil. When creating a new `EmbeddableHost` without assigning `host` first (e.g., `EmbeddableHost.new` followed by validation), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass`. Add a guard like `self.host&.sub!(...)` or check for presence.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation on host column
findings.body: The `EmbeddableHost` model has no uniqueness validation on the `host` attribute, and the migration does not add a unique index. This allows duplicate host entries to be created, which could cause ambiguous lookups in `record_for_host` (it uses `.first` so it picks an arbitrary one) and confusing admin UI behavior.

findings.title: create_table uses force: true which drops existing table
findings.body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will silently drop the `embeddable_hosts` table if it already exists, destroying any data. This is unusual for a migration and dangerous if the migration is re-run or if the table was created by another means. Use `create_table` without `force: true` and handle the existing-table case explicitly if needed.

findings.title: update action is a no-op that doesn't persist any changes
findings.body: The `update` action in `Admin::EmbeddingController` simply re-serializes the current embedding without applying any changes from the request. The frontend calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` which hits this endpoint. While individual host saves go through `EmbeddableHostsController`, this endpoint gives the false impression that it does something. If it's intentionally a no-op placeholder, it should be documented or removed.
